transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I suppose what brings me in is that I’ve been noticing, over the past year or so, that I’m just always doing something. Puttering around the house, fixing little things, rearranging things, saying yes to one more volunteer job… nothing terrible, I don’t think, but even at my age, I seem to have a hard time just sitting down and being still. I’m not sure if that’s the sort of thing you mean, but it’s been on my mind.
When this happens, do you find that you need less sleep than usual?

I don’t think so, no… at least, I haven’t noticed needing less sleep in any clear way. I mean, my sleep isn’t something I’ve been tracking carefully, but I wouldn’t say I’m suddenly fine on very little sleep or anything like that. Does that answer what you mean?
When you’re staying busy like that, is it because your mind is filled with worry?

I wouldn’t say it’s worry, exactly… at least not that I’m aware of. I’m sure I have ordinary concerns like anyone, but when I’m busy like that it feels more like I just sort of keep moving from one thing to the next. I don’t know if that makes sense.
When you keep moving from one task to the next, do you feel a strong need to do things a certain way?

Hmm… no, I don’t think so. Not in a strong way, anyway. I mean, I have my little preferences, like anyone does, but I wouldn’t say I feel driven to do things a certain exact way. It’s more that I just move on to the next thing before I’ve really settled, if that makes sense.
Have you had trouble paying attention since you were a child?

Yes… I think so, looking back. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but in grade school I do remember being scolded for popping out of my seat or talking over other children. Teachers would say I was “too lively,” that sort of thing, long before I was a teenager. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do these attention or restlessness problems cause trouble for you in day-to-day life?

A little, yes… though I don’t want to overstate it. At the senior center, there have been a few times after meetings where I felt I needed to apologize. And one friend, very kindly, suggested maybe I take a smaller role at the sign-up table because my manner was making things a bit tense. I felt badly about that. Does that count as trouble in day-to-day life?
Have there been times when you felt unusually cheerful or high for several days in a row?

I don’t think so, no. I’ve had good moods, of course, or days where I’m pleased about something, but not unusually high for several days in a row… at least not that I’ve noticed. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
For long stretches of time, have you felt down or depressed most days?
No, I wouldn’t say that. I mean, I have my sad days like anyone my age, I suppose, but not long stretches where I’m down most days. At least, nothing I’d call depressed… does that answer it?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a lifelong pattern of hyperactivity/restlessness and probable inattention beginning in childhood, with ongoing symptoms into older adulthood and mild but real social/role impairment. The interview also argues against mood episodes, generalized worry, compulsive behavior, and depression as better explanations. Given the limited subtype detail but persistent ADHD-type symptoms, the best fitting ICD-10 diagnosis is F90.9.
